head: A brewer lost a bet
and built a bestseller.
slides.sub: How a question about a bird became a book in every home.

image.label: A pint-strewn pub table with an open thick book
image.brief: 1950년대 아일랜드 펍의 나무 테이블. 흑맥주 잔 두 개 옆에 펼쳐진 두꺼운 책. 따뜻한 램프 조명과 담배 연기. 실제 맥주 상표나 로고 없음.

head: A cold shoot in Wexford.
A bird gets away.
body: In 1951, Sir Hugh Beaver, the managing director of the Guinness brewery, was at a shooting party in the marshes of County Wexford, Ireland.
A flight of birds was too quick for the guns. That night, the group argued: which was Europe's fastest game bird?

image.label: Hunters in tweed on a misty Irish marsh at dawn
image.brief: 새벽 안개 낀 아일랜드 습지. 트위드 차림 사냥꾼들의 실루엣 뒤로 빠르게 날아가는 새 떼. 얼굴은 보이지 않게.

head: Every book in the house.
No answer.
body: The choice was between the golden plover and the red grouse. In a story often told, they searched reference books and found nothing that settled it.
Beaver saw something bigger. If his friends argued over facts like this, so did people in pubs every night.

image.label: A country house library with books piled open
image.brief: 시골 저택 서재. 펼쳐진 백과사전과 조류 도감이 탁자에 쌓여 있고 벽난로 불빛이 비침.

head: You sell beer, not books.
What do you do?
body: You run a big brewery. You have an idea for a book of facts that could end pub arguments.

options.text: Print a short free leaflet of fun facts, packed with beer ads
options.feedback: Cheap and on-brand. But people throw away ads, and nobody trusts a leaflet to settle a bet. Keep swiping.

options.text: Drop it and stick to brewing, the business you know
options.feedback: Safe and focused. It also leaves a gap that someone else might fill. Keep swiping.

options.text: Hire serious researchers and make a real reference book with your name on it
options.feedback: It costs time and money outside your core business, with no promise of sales. Keep swiping.

image.label: A 1950s office desk with a beer bottle and a blank notebook
image.brief: 1950년대 양조회사 임원 사무실 책상. 상표 없는 맥주병 하나와 빈 노트, 만년필. 창밖은 더블린풍 벽돌 건물.

head: He didn't want ads.
He wanted facts.
body: Beaver was introduced to Norris and Ross McWhirter, twin brothers who ran a fact-finding agency in London. They supplied facts and figures to newspapers.
Guinness set up a company to make the book, and the twins got to work checking records of every kind.

image.label: Two silhouetted men at desks buried in papers and files
image.brief: 런던 작은 사무실, 서류와 파일에 파묻혀 일하는 두 남자의 뒷모습 실루엣. 1950년대 타자기와 전화기.

slides.label: pages in the first edition, published on 27 August 1955
body: It covered the tallest, fastest, oldest and biggest in nature, science, sport and more. The Guinness name sat on the cover, but the pages were about the facts.

image.label: A stack of plain green hardback books fresh from the press
image.brief: 인쇄소에서 막 나온 단색 양장본 책 더미. 1950년대 인쇄기 배경. 실제 책 표지 디자인이나 로고는 따라 하지 않음.

head: Printed as a promotion.
Sold as a bestseller.
body: According to the company, by Christmas 1955 the book topped the British bestseller list.
People bought it to settle arguments, then kept reading it for fun. New editions followed, and the book was updated again and again.

image.label: A crowded 1950s bookshop window at Christmas
image.brief: 1950년대 크리스마스 시즌 영국 서점 진열창. 같은 책이 피라미드처럼 쌓여 있고 창밖에 눈과 외투 입은 행인들.

head: The beer was never
the point of the page.
body: A book full of ads would have been tossed aside. A trusted book of facts stayed on shelves, in pubs and in homes for years.
Each time someone opened it to win a bet, they saw the Guinness name.

image.label: Two people in a pub leaning over a book to settle a bet
image.brief: 펍 카운터에서 책을 펼쳐 들고 내기를 확인하는 두 사람의 뒷모습. 한 명은 손을 들어 이긴 표정을 짓는 실루엣.

head: Solve a real job,
and the brand rides along.
body: Pub-goers had a clear job: end an argument with a fact everyone would accept. Beaver built something that did that job well, rather than one more advert.
Useful content became an asset people paid for, kept and shared, carrying the name further than paid ads could.

image.label: A book with light glowing from its open pages
image.brief: 펼쳐진 책 페이지에서 빛이 퍼져 나오는 그래픽. 어두운 배경, 단순한 구성.

head: Listen to what people argue
then answer it better.
body: The questions your customers keep asking can become something they value on its own.
**Try it today:** write down three questions customers argue about or ask you often. Could you answer one so well that people would keep it?

image.label: An empty pub table at closing time with one book left on it
image.brief: 영업이 끝난 펍의 빈 테이블 위에 놓인 책 한 권. 의자는 올려져 있고 조명은 은은하게.

factChecks.note: 사냥 모임의 시기(1951년 11월)와 장소(아일랜드 웩스퍼드주 North Slob), 골든 플로버와 붉은뇌조 중 어느 새가 더 빠른지에 대한 논쟁은 Guinness World Records 공식 연혁 기준입니다. 카드에는 날짜를 적지 않고 1951년만 적었습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 1951년 11월 10일 웩스퍼드 North Slob 사냥, 골든 플로버 논쟁 확인(5월로 적은 자료도 있음).
Sir Hugh Beaver가 당시 Guinness 양조장의 managing director였다는 점, 참고 서적에서 답을 찾지 못했다는 일화는 공식 연혁에 나오지만 전해지는 이야기 성격이 있어 "a story often told"로 표시했습니다.
Norris·Ross McWhirter 쌍둥이가 런던에서 사실 조사 에이전시를 운영했고, Guinness 직원이던 Christopher Chataway의 소개로 연결되었다는 점을 공식 연혁과 McWhirter 관련 자료로 확인하세요. 카드에는 Chataway 이름을 넣지 않았습니다.
초판 발행일(1955년 8월 27일)과 198쪽 분량은 Guinness World Records 공식 자료 기준입니다. 쪽수가 자료마다 다르면 stat 슬라이드 숫자를 바꾸세요. → [2026-11-02 확인] 1955년 8월 27일 198쪽 초판 확인(197쪽으로 적은 자료도 있음).
"1955년 크리스마스 무렵 영국 베스트셀러 1위"는 회사 연혁에 나오는 주장이라 "according to the company"로 표시했습니다. 판매 부수는 넣지 않았습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 1955년 크리스마스 무렵 영국 베스트셀러 1위 확인.
영국 내 펍 수(약 8만 1천 곳으로 흔히 인용됨) 등 추가 숫자는 확실하지 않아 넣지 않았습니다. 초판 일부를 펍에 무료 배포했다는 이야기도 확인되지 않아 뺐습니다.
